recoveryCoverage: Persisted pending admission before merge remains pending and does not execute Git on retry.
Persisted pending admission after merge becomes applied by observing the exact clean candidate HEAD without invoking a post-merge hook again.
Dirty destinations remain pending; new request identities cannot replace unresolved admission.
Applied request retries preserve the original receipt; changed request revision or SHA is rejected.
Application bookkeeping leaves the accepted task proof hash unchanged and survives ordinary task writes.
New applications reject clean but changed source and target SHAs before durable admission.
Goal policy requires matching applied receipts and blocks pending applications even on cancelled tasks.
limits: Recovery tests construct persisted before/after-merge boundaries; they do not kill a real server while a Git child or hook remains alive.
Ambiguous admitted operations require explicit host reconciliation; no automatic abandon or replay is implemented.
Local per-project host locking and in-process assignment serialization do not fence external Git commands or coordinate across hosts.
No exactly-once claim is made for Git hooks or other external effects.
Agents UI, cross-host application and broader upstream feature parity remain pending.
